definitions.gloss: to wear out through use; to use until worn and old
definitions.explanation: To use something so much or for so long that it becomes old, shabby, or no longer in good condition. Can also apply figuratively to ideas or expressions that have become stale from overuse.

examples.japanese: {使|つか}い{古|ふる}した⟦タオル→タオル：01533_taoru⟧。
{使|つか}い{古|ふる}した⟦{辞書|じしょ}→辞書：04707_jisho⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ボロボロだ。
examples.english: My well-worn dictionary is falling apart.

examples.japanese: {使|つか}い{古|ふる}された⟦{表現|ひょうげん}→表現：03584_hyougen⟧⟦ではなく→ではなく：09578_dehanaku⟧、⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}き→書く：00477_kaku⟧⟦なさい→なさる：01307_nasaru⟧。
examples.english: Write in your own words, not with worn-out clichés.

notes:
A compound verb from ⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧ (to use) + {古|ふる}す (to make old through use). Most commonly encountered in the past participle form {使|つか}い{古|ふる}した (worn-out, well-used) modifying nouns.

USAGE:
The form {使|つか}い{古|ふる}した functions as a common adjective-like modifier. Can carry either a negative nuance (shabby, past its prime) or a positive one (well-loved, seasoned). The passive form {使|つか}い{古|ふる}された is used for figurative contexts like clichés.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {使|つか}い{古|ふる}した⟦タオル→タオル：01533_taoru⟧ — a worn-out towel
- {使|つか}い{古|ふる}した⟦{道具|どうぐ}→道具：01479_dougu⟧ — well-worn tools
- {使|つか}い{古|ふる}された⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧ — hackneyed words, clichés
- {使|つか}い{古|ふる}した⟦{靴|くつ}→靴：00725_kutsu⟧ — worn-out shoes

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{擦|す}り{減|へ}る→擦り減る：17261_suriheru⟧ — to wear down, to be worn away (physical erosion)
- ⟦くたびれる→くたびれる：28755_kutabireru⟧ — to become tired/worn (also used for people and things)
- ボロボロ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ — to become tattered, to fall apart (more extreme deterioration)
